messages:
ana: Quick sync — I ran a cross-GPU sweep focused on two knobs: batch window (20ms/50ms/100ms) vs max_batch_tokens (256/1024/2048). Regions: us-west1, eu-west1, ap-northeast1. Wanted to surface the outliers and kernel-choice notes.

sam: Nice. TL;DR numbers?

ana: TL;DR first: H100 has best median latency for large max_tokens at 50ms window. A100 throughput slightly better at 100ms for 1024 tokens. T4 is only viable at low tokens and small window.

riya: Can you paste the command you used and the raw table?

ana: Sure, command we used (simplified):
```bash
./perf_sweep --model mosaic-13b-v1 --gpus h100,a100,t4 --regions us-west1,eu-west1,ap-northeast1 --window_ms 20,50,100 --max_tokens 256,1024,2048 --requests 10000 --workload continuous-batch
```
Raw CSV snippet (median latency ms, p95 ms, tokens/s):
```
gpu,region,window_ms,max_tokens,median_ms,p95_ms,tokens_per_sec
H100,us-west1,20,256,48,120,2100
H100,us-west1,50,1024,62,150,5200
H100,us-west1,100,2048,90,320,7800
A100,eu-west1,20,256,60,140,1800
A100,eu-west1,50,1024,70,180,5600
A100,eu-west1,100,2048,95,350,8200
T4,ap-northeast1,20,256,85,300,400
T4,ap-northeast1,50,1024,140,620,900
```

sam: Hm p95 for T4 is brutal for high tokens — expected. Any kernel mismatch warnings?

lee: For H100 runs I saw the runtime choose the big-gemm kernel for 2048 in us-west1; in eu-west1 it picked the split-kernel path (smaller GEMM + rematerialize) — likely due to library version difference on the host image. That explains some of the cross-region variance.

ana: Good catch. I pinned the CUDA/cuBLAS versions but apparently NCCL/ML library minor diffs remain. I'll re-run with a forced kernel selection flag to confirm.

perf-bot: Automated note: 1718250123 — background quantization job (mosaic-13b-8bit) started on staging.

riya: Any notes on fairness? We measured cold-start tail for multi-tenant mix?

ana: Yes — we ran a 70/30 read/write mix with priority decay enabled. Observations: smaller windows (20ms) improve SLAs for low-token requests (<=256) but reduce aggregate tokens/sec for high-token requests; large windows (100ms) increase throughput but cause 99th latency spikes for low-priority tenants.

sam: Do we have a recommended knob map for customers? e.g., latency-sensitive vs throughput-sensitive profiles?

ana: Draft recommendations: 
- Latency-sensitive (chat): window_ms=20, max_batch_tokens=256, prefer H100 if available.
- Balanced (completion API): window_ms=50, max_batch_tokens=1024, can use A100 for cost/perf.
- Throughput-heavy (bulk embedding/long completions): window_ms=100, max_batch_tokens=2048, prefer H100 or A100 with tuned kernels.

lee: Also note autoscaler warmup_jitter needs to be conservative when using large windows — otherwise we see microburst coalescing during scale events that increases p95.

riya: Any regression vs last week's quantized model? We care about quality drift when using cont-batcher + 8-bit quant.

ana: Quick eval: BLEU-like proxy + a small eval set. 8-bit quant model had <0.8% quality regression on the long completion set at 1024 tokens. For smaller short-turn prompts (<=256) regression negligible.

sam: Can you attach the perf plots?

ana: I uploaded the three PNGs to the perf dashboard (link): https://perf.redwood.internal/bench/1718250000-window-sweep — includes median/p95/tokens-per-sec across axes.

perf-bot: 1718250345 — submitted benchmark artifacts to S3: s3://redwood-perf/benchmarks/1718250000/ (csv + plots).

1) ana to re-run H100/eu-west1 forcing kernel flag and post new CSV (ETA today EOD).
2) sam to draft knob recommendations for the public docs based on the three profiles above.
3) riya to run the quality regression eval with the latest 8-bit build across the three windows and post delta report.

ana: Noted — I expect the canary to show improved chat latency but may see a small throughput dip. Monitoring dashboards alerted on p95 in canary when we tried 20ms last month — watch for that.
